purpose: Negative vectors for the action-ref timestamp grammar gate. A conformant verifier MUST reject any timestamp that is not canonical RFC 3339 UTC written with ASCII digits [0-9], three fractional digits and a mandatory Z, before any hashing. A timestamp that uses non-ASCII decimal digits is not a valid form even when it looks like one.
validation_rule: The grammar gate runs before canonicalization. A timestamp that fails the gate is a terminal failure before invocation. A verifier that accepts any vector in this file has a conformance bug.

reserved_slots.requirement: A negative vector whose timestamp uses non-ASCII decimal digits in place of [0-9] in an otherwise canonical RFC 3339 string. Must be rejected at the grammar gate.
reserved_slots.note: Filled by the contributed vector neg-0001-arabic-indic-digits.

vectors.description: The invocation payload carries the canonical RFC 3339 instant written with Arabic-Indic digits (U+0660 to U+0669) in place of ASCII [0-9]. A grammar written with \d accepts it, because Python's \d matches any Unicode decimal digit. The claimed action_ref is the real digest of that payload, so a verifier that skips the grammar gate and hashes verbatim would see a match. A conformant verifier rejects the timestamp at the grammar gate before hashing and never normalizes the digits to retry.
vectors.expected: rejected at the timestamp grammar gate, before canonicalization or hashing
vectors.provenance: contributed by aeoess (Agent Passport System), follow-up to PR #115. Same tuple as recompute-drift-v1 neg-b01 with the timestamp digits replaced
